participants.note: Concept ACKed, but raised multiple objections regarding silent error ignoring and failures when running CI locally under Podman
Concept ACKed, but raised concerns that host background daemons could trigger false-positive CI failures
ACKed an earlier commit after testing with non-loopback DNS servers in CI
Concept ACK, citing privacy risks of tests leaking developer IP addresses
Previously tested and ACKed, but has an open objection regarding tcpdump --direction being a no-op when reading files
Opposed merging while local CI runs under Podman fail due to outbound network traffic
Concept ACK and tested on Cirrus workers
Reviewed and ACKed multiple revisions, suggested test setup improvements, and reported a filter bug that was fixed

claims.harm: False-positive CI failures if unrelated background daemons on the CI host VM generate network traffic
claims.quote: i'm slightly worried this may generate false positive. As is, this detects traffic on the entire (virtual) machine while running the tests. Are there no other daemons running on the CI instance that could interfere with this?
claims.settled_by_quote: About the false positives - I think it is worth trying this in its current mode where any detected traffic is assumed to have originated from the tests and fails the CI.

claims.harm: tcpdump buffers output when writing to a file, causing captured packets to be missed when the file is read
claims.quote: I don't think this works reliably? See: ... Use the -U flag to cause packets to be written as soon as they are received.

claims.harm: Silently ignoring return codes and omitting pipefail allows broken network detection to pass CI silently
claims.quote: Ignoring the return code in all tasks can mean that even the tasks where the detection is working are going to silently break tomorrow. As mentioned previously in the thread you closed, I think this is brittle.
claims.settled_by_quote: Enabled `pipefail` as in the above diff. Thanks!

claims.harm: CI scripts fail when run locally under Podman due to external DNS traffic, breaking supported local test workflows
claims.quote: Yea, I have seen the same, on one of my Fedora boxes, which would be a blocker, given it breaks running the CI locally.
claims.settled_by_quote: with the addition of `-dnsseed=0` this should be robust and work as intended on docker or podman, locally or in CI cloud.

claims.harm: Non-deterministic false-positive test failures during local CI runs under Podman
claims.quote: The current failures are non-deterministic, which is a blocker to merging this. We have enough intermittent issues already, and I don't think it is a good use of time to add more, when there isn't even enough time to track and deal with the existing ones.
claims.settled_by_quote: with the addition of `-dnsseed=0` this should be robust and work as intended on docker or podman, locally or in CI cloud.

claims.harm: filter variable is not reset for non-loopback interfaces and persists across invocations, which could ignore non-port-53 traffic
claims.quote: Looks like there is a bug here because `filter` variable is not reset if `ifname` does not begin with "lo". Also filter is not declared as a local variable so it will persist between calls.

claims.harm: tcpdump --direction is only enforced during packet capture and acts as a no-op when reading files, failing to filter direction
claims.quote: It seems that `--direction` is only enforced at capture time, so it should be moved to the tcpdump call in `traffic_monitor_begin()`. Or maybe just delete here if we don't want to filter there because here it seems to be no op.

support.reason: it turns out the owners of 1.2.3.4, 11.22.33.44 and 8.8.8.8, if they would bother, would know the IP address of every dev who runs the functional tests at home.
Nice solution to use `127.0.0.1:1` as unreachable proxy for DNS requests too. I ran this on my CI runners with a 8.8.8.8 and 1.1.1.1 as DNS servers as before and the tests don't connect out now.
The changes in the tests look good but I need a little more time with the CI stuff.

I tested this with https://github.com/Sjors/bitcoin/pull/76 on my own CI setup, which uses Cirrus workers configured using (roughly) the instructions here: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/.cirrus.yml#L8 (using podman-docker)
The new tcpdump mechanism to detect unexpected traffic is pretty simple and seems very nice.
Just rebased since last review and replaced node_init_tests fix CreateSock fix with natpmp=0 fix
just dropping INTERNET_TRAFFIC_EXPECTED variable since last review
just documenting things better since last review and adding missing exit 1 to trigger CI failure (nice find!)
Tested again by pushing the latest version of the code with the change of the first commit commented out. I could observe the expected failure in the CI this time
Since last review just rebased to avoid conflicts, added comments to commit message and test, added `local` to some bash variables
I think there is value here, re-Concept ACK, to clarify.

result.notes: Initial record update for PR #31349. Earlier blockers raised by fanquake and maflcko regarding Podman failures and DNS seed lookups were resolved after tests were configured to run with -dnsseed=0, leaving an open concern from fjahr regarding the misuse of tcpdump's --direction flag when reading packet captures.
